quests.definition: 'Settle down' means to become calm and stable, especially after a period of moving around or living an unsettled lifestyle, often associated with starting a stable home life.
quests.exampleSentence: After years of traveling, she finally decided to settle DOWN and buy a house.
quests.example: After years of traveling, she finally decided to settle DOWN and buy a house.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'DOWN' combines with the verb 'SETTLE' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative: nothing physically lowers — the phrase describes a life becoming calmer and more stable over time.
quests.nativeTip: This means becoming calm and stable in life, often after a period of change or travel.
quests.visualAnchor: 🗝️ SETTLE + DOWN ➔ SETTLE DOWN

quests.definition: 'Settle in' means to become comfortable in a new place or situation, such as a new job or home, as the initial unfamiliarity fades.
quests.exampleSentence: It took the new employee a few weeks to settle IN at the office.
quests.example: It took the new employee a few weeks to settle IN at the office.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'IN' combines with the verb 'SETTLE' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative: nothing physically enters anything — the phrase describes gradually becoming comfortable in new surroundings.
quests.nativeTip: This means becoming comfortable and adjusted to new surroundings or a new routine.
quests.visualAnchor: 🗝️ SETTLE + IN ➔ SETTLE IN

quests.definition: 'Settled down' fits life becoming calm and stable overall, a step beyond 'settling in' to new surroundings, which describes the earlier adjustment period.
quests.exampleSentence: Now that they've settled DOWN into a stable daily routine, life feels much calmer.
quests.example: Now that they've settled DOWN into a stable daily routine, life feels much calmer.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'DOWN' combines with the verb 'SETTLE' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative, as before — the phrase describes life reaching a calm, stable rhythm.
quests.nativeTip: This means daily life becoming genuinely calm and stable, beyond simply adjusting to new surroundings.
quests.visualAnchor: 🗝️ SETTLE + DOWN ➔ SETTLE DOWN

quests.definition: 'Wind down' means to relax and gradually release tension after being busy or stressed, often through a calming activity.
quests.exampleSentence: After a stressful week, she likes to wind DOWN with a good book.
quests.example: After a stressful week, she likes to wind DOWN with a good book.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'DOWN' combines with the verb 'WIND' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative, borrowing the image of a mechanism slowly running out of energy and coming to a gentle stop.
quests.nativeTip: This means relaxing and easing tension after a busy or stressful period.
quests.visualAnchor: 🗝️ WIND + DOWN ➔ WIND DOWN

quests.definition: 'Wind up (somewhere or in some situation)' means to end up there, often unexpectedly or as an unintended consequence of earlier choices.
quests.exampleSentence: If you're not careful with money, you could wind UP in serious debt.
quests.example: If you're not careful with money, you could wind UP in serious debt.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'UP' combines with the verb 'WIND' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative, borrowing the image of a mechanism winding forward to an unplanned final position.
quests.nativeTip: This means ending up in a particular situation, often without having planned for it.
quests.visualAnchor: 🗝️ WIND + UP ➔ WIND UP

quests.definition: This contrasts with 'wind down' from earlier in this level — instead of the planned relaxation, he unexpectedly 'wound up' doing the opposite: working even later.
quests.exampleSentence: Instead of winding down after the long shift, he somehow wound UP working even later into the night.
quests.example: Instead of winding down after the long shift, he somehow wound UP working even later into the night.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'UP' combines with the verb 'WIND' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative, as before — the phrase describes ending up in an unplanned situation.
quests.nativeTip: This means unexpectedly ending up doing more work, rather than relaxing as intended.
quests.visualAnchor: 🗝️ WIND + UP ➔ WIND UP

quests.definition: 'Ease up' means to reduce effort, intensity, or pressure, often to allow for rest, recovery, or a less stressful pace.
quests.exampleSentence: The coach told the team to ease UP during recovery week.
quests.example: The coach told the team to ease UP during recovery week.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'UP' combines with the verb 'EASE' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative: nothing physically becomes easier to lift — the phrase describes intentionally reducing pressure or effort.
quests.nativeTip: This means reducing effort or intensity, especially to allow rest or recovery.
quests.visualAnchor: 🗝️ EASE + UP ➔ EASE UP

quests.definition: 'Ease up on' fits reducing pressure placed on someone else, such as unrealistic deadlines for employees, distinct from 'slow down,' which usually describes reducing your own pace.
quests.exampleSentence: Rather than simply slowing down his own pace, the manager needed to EASE UP on his employees' unrealistic deadlines.
quests.example: Rather than simply slowing down his own pace, the manager needed to EASE UP on his employees' unrealistic deadlines.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'EASE UP' combines with the verb 'EASE' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative, as before — the phrase describes reducing pressure or demands placed on someone else.
quests.nativeTip: This means reducing pressure placed on other people, rather than just slowing your own personal pace.
quests.visualAnchor: 🗝️ EASE + EASE UP ➔ EASE EASE UP

quests.definition: This reinforces 'ease up,' here as a request to reduce harsh criticism toward someone already putting in genuine effort.
quests.exampleSentence: Could you ease UP on the criticism? He's already doing his best.
quests.example: Could you ease UP on the criticism? He's already doing his best.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'UP' combines with the verb 'EASE' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative, as before — the phrase describes reducing pressure or harshness directed at someone.
quests.nativeTip: This means being less harshly critical toward someone who is already trying their best.
quests.visualAnchor: 🗝️ EASE + UP ➔ EASE UP

quests.definition: This draws on the full range of GET meanings taught throughout the curriculum. Recovering emotionally after a painful experience points clearly to 'get over,' distinct from 'get by' (manage with little), 'get away' (escape), or 'get ahead' (progress in a career).
quests.exampleSentence: After the divorce, it took him nearly a year to really GET OVER the emotional pain and start dating again.
quests.example: After the divorce, it took him nearly a year to really GET OVER the emotional pain and start dating again.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'GET OVER' combines with the verb 'GET' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative, as before — the phrase describes recovering emotionally from something difficult.
quests.nativeTip: This means emotionally recovering from a painful experience, not managing with little money or escaping a place.
quests.visualAnchor: 🗝️ GET + GET OVER ➔ GET GET OVER

quests.definition: 'Get by' fits managing to survive on very limited income, distinct from 'get over' (emotional recovery), 'get away' (escape), and 'get ahead' (career progress).
quests.exampleSentence: Despite earning very little, the young couple somehow managed to GET BY during their first year of marriage.
quests.example: Despite earning very little, the young couple somehow managed to GET BY during their first year of marriage.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'GET BY' combines with the verb 'GET' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative, as before — the phrase describes managing adequately despite limited resources.
quests.nativeTip: This means managing to survive financially despite very limited income, not recovering emotionally or making career progress.
quests.visualAnchor: 🗝️ GET + GET BY ➔ GET GET BY

quests.definition: 'Get along' fits describing a friendly, harmonious relationship despite differences, distinct from 'get by' (financial survival), 'get over' (emotional recovery), and 'get away' (escape).
quests.exampleSentence: The two roommates couldn't be more different, yet they GET ALONG surprisingly well.
quests.example: The two roommates couldn't be more different, yet they GET ALONG surprisingly well.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'GET ALONG' combines with the verb 'GET' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative, as before — the phrase describes a cooperative, friendly relationship between two people.
quests.nativeTip: This means having a friendly, harmonious relationship, not managing financially or recovering from something difficult.
quests.visualAnchor: 🗝️ GET + GET ALONG ➔ GET GET ALONG

quests.definition: This draws on the full range of TAKE meanings taught throughout the curriculum. Assuming control of a family business points clearly to 'take over,' distinct from 'take up' (start a hobby), 'take on' (accept responsibility), and 'take back' (retract a statement).
quests.exampleSentence: After the founder's sudden resignation, his daughter had to TAKE OVER the family business much sooner than planned.
quests.example: After the founder's sudden resignation, his daughter had to TAKE OVER the family business much sooner than planned.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'TAKE OVER' combines with the verb 'TAKE' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative, as before — the phrase describes assuming control of an organization.
quests.nativeTip: This means assuming control of a business, not starting a hobby, accepting new responsibility, or retracting a statement.
quests.visualAnchor: 🗝️ TAKE + TAKE OVER ➔ TAKE TAKE OVER

quests.definition: 'Take up' fits starting a completely new hobby in retirement, distinct from 'take over' (assume control), 'take on' (accept responsibility), and 'take out' (remove or dine out).
quests.exampleSentence: Retirement gave him plenty of free time, so he decided to TAKE UP painting as a new hobby.
quests.example: Retirement gave him plenty of free time, so he decided to TAKE UP painting as a new hobby.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'TAKE UP' combines with the verb 'TAKE' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative, as before — the phrase describes beginning a new activity or interest.
quests.nativeTip: This means starting a brand-new hobby, not assuming control, accepting a task, or retracting words.
quests.visualAnchor: 🗝️ TAKE + TAKE UP ➔ TAKE TAKE UP

quests.definition: 'Take back' fits withdrawing a hurtful statement, distinct from 'take up' (start a hobby), 'take over' (assume control), and 'take on' (accept responsibility).
quests.exampleSentence: Realizing she'd spoken too harshly, she quickly tried to TAKE BACK her hurtful comment.
quests.example: Realizing she'd spoken too harshly, she quickly tried to TAKE BACK her hurtful comment.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'TAKE BACK' combines with the verb 'TAKE' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative, as before — the phrase describes retracting something said in haste or anger.
quests.nativeTip: This means withdrawing a statement made in haste, not starting a hobby, assuming control, or accepting responsibility.
quests.visualAnchor: 🗝️ TAKE + TAKE BACK ➔ TAKE TAKE BACK

quests.definition: This draws on the full range of BREAK meanings taught throughout the curriculum. Failed trade negotiations point clearly to 'broke down,' distinct from 'broke up' (ended a relationship), 'broke out' (began suddenly), and 'broke into' (entered by force).
quests.exampleSentence: Negotiations between the two nations finally BROKE DOWN after neither side would compromise on trade terms.
quests.example: Negotiations between the two nations finally BROKE DOWN after neither side would compromise on trade terms.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'BROKE DOWN' combines with the verb 'BREAK' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative, as before — the phrase describes negotiations or talks failing to reach agreement.
quests.nativeTip: This means negotiations failing entirely, not a relationship ending, a sudden event starting, or forced entry.
quests.visualAnchor: 🗝️ BREAK + BROKE DOWN ➔ BREAK BROKE DOWN

quests.definition: 'Fell apart' fits a sudden, dramatic ending, matching 'almost overnight,' distinct from 'grew apart' (a slow, quiet drift), 'broke up' (which would need a differently structured sentence here), and 'fell through' (a plan failing to happen).
quests.exampleSentence: Their marriage of fifteen years FELL APART almost overnight after the affair was discovered.
quests.example: Their marriage of fifteen years FELL APART almost overnight after the affair was discovered.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'FELL APART' combines with the verb 'FALL' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative, as before — the phrase describes a relationship suddenly collapsing rather than fading slowly.
quests.nativeTip: This means a relationship ending suddenly and dramatically, not gradually and quietly, or a plan simply failing to happen.
quests.visualAnchor: 🗝️ FALL + FELL APART ➔ FALL FELL APART

quests.definition: 'Fell through' fits a plan collapsing at a late stage due to an external cause, distinct from 'fell apart' (a relationship or object collapsing), 'fell behind' (losing pace), and 'fell short' (failing to meet a standard).
quests.exampleSentence: Their long-planned wedding FELL THROUGH when the venue unexpectedly canceled the booking.
quests.example: Their long-planned wedding FELL THROUGH when the venue unexpectedly canceled the booking.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'FELL THROUGH' combines with the verb 'FALL' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative, as before — the phrase describes a plan collapsing before it could be completed.
quests.nativeTip: This means a plan failing to happen at a late stage, not a relationship collapsing, losing pace, or failing to meet a standard.
quests.visualAnchor: 🗝️ FALL + FELL THROUGH ➔ FALL FELL THROUGH

quests.definition: This draws on the full range of COME meanings taught throughout the curriculum. An unexpected new problem arising points clearly to 'came up,' distinct from 'came across' (found by chance or gave an impression), 'came round' (changed opinion), and 'came over' (visited).
quests.exampleSentence: Just as everyone thought the crisis was over, a new problem suddenly CAME UP that changed everything.
quests.example: Just as everyone thought the crisis was over, a new problem suddenly CAME UP that changed everything.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'CAME UP' combines with the verb 'COME' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative, as before — the phrase describes an unexpected problem or event arising suddenly.
quests.nativeTip: This means an unexpected new problem arising, not a chance discovery, a change of opinion, or a casual visit.
quests.visualAnchor: 🗝️ COME + CAME UP ➔ COME CAME UP

quests.definition: 'Came round' fits gradually accepting an idea after initial resistance, distinct from 'came up' (an unexpected event), 'came across' (chance discovery), and 'came over' (a visit).
quests.exampleSentence: It took him a long time, but he eventually CAME ROUND to accepting the new schedule.
quests.example: It took him a long time, but he eventually CAME ROUND to accepting the new schedule.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'CAME ROUND' combines with the verb 'COME' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative, as before — the phrase describes gradually accepting an idea after initial resistance.
quests.nativeTip: This means gradually accepting an idea you initially opposed, not an unexpected problem arising, a chance discovery, or a casual visit.
quests.visualAnchor: 🗝️ COME + CAME ROUND ➔ COME CAME ROUND

quests.definition: 'Go through with' fits actually carrying out a plan despite a setback, especially one you might otherwise abandon. 'Go along with' means complying with someone else's idea, and 'go on with' would mean simply continuing, without the extra sense of overcoming hesitation.
quests.exampleSentence: Despite the setback, the team agreed to go THROUGH WITH the original plan rather than abandon it.
quests.example: Despite the setback, the team agreed to go THROUGH WITH the original plan rather than abandon it.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'THROUGH WITH' combines with the verb 'GO' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative, as before — the phrase describes overcoming hesitation to complete something despite a setback.
quests.nativeTip: This means actually carrying out the original plan despite a setback, not simply continuing, complying, or being well received.
quests.visualAnchor: 🗝️ GO + THROUGH WITH ➔ GO THROUGH WITH

quests.definition: 'Looked up to' fits continued admiration despite a scandal, distinct from 'look down on' (disrespect), 'look after' (care for), and simply 'look on' (watch without involvement).
quests.exampleSentence: Even though the scandal was public knowledge, some young fans still looked UP TO him as a hero.
quests.example: Even though the scandal was public knowledge, some young fans still looked UP TO him as a hero.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'UP TO' combines with the verb 'LOOK' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative, as before — the phrase describes ongoing admiration despite reasons to feel otherwise.
quests.nativeTip: This means continuing to admire someone despite public knowledge of their wrongdoing, not regarding them with disrespect or caretaking them.
quests.visualAnchor: 🗝️ LOOK + UP TO ➔ LOOK UP TO

quests.definition: 'Stood out' fits being noticeably impressive compared to others, distinct from 'stood by' (remained loyal), 'stood for' (represented a value or refused to tolerate something), and 'stood up' (rose physically).
quests.exampleSentence: During the crisis, it was the quiet accountant, not the flashy executives, who really STOOD OUT when everyone else panicked.
quests.example: During the crisis, it was the quiet accountant, not the flashy executives, who really STOOD OUT when everyone else panicked.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'STOOD OUT' combines with the verb 'STAND' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative, as before — the phrase describes being distinctly more impressive than others nearby.
quests.nativeTip: This means being noticeably impressive compared to others in the room, not remaining loyal, representing a value, or rising physically.
quests.visualAnchor: 🗝️ STAND + STOOD OUT ➔ STAND STOOD OUT

quests.definition: 'Play down' fits deliberately using softer language, like 'strategic restructuring,' to minimize how serious layoffs sound, distinct from 'play up' (exaggerate), 'spell out' (explain explicitly), and 'gloss over' (give insufficient attention, without necessarily reframing the language itself).
quests.exampleSentence: The company's press release clearly tried to PLAY DOWN the seriousness of the layoffs, calling them a 'strategic restructuring.'
quests.example: The company's press release clearly tried to PLAY DOWN the seriousness of the layoffs, calling them a 'strategic restructuring.'
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'PLAY DOWN' combines with the verb 'PLAY' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative, as before — the phrase describes deliberately understating something's seriousness through careful word choice.
quests.nativeTip: This means using softer, more pleasant language to minimize how serious something sounds, not exaggerating it, explaining it explicitly, or briefly skipping past it.
quests.visualAnchor: 🗝️ PLAY + PLAY DOWN ➔ PLAY PLAY DOWN

quests.definition: This integrates the negotiation cluster from earlier in the curriculum into one realistic, drawn-out committee scenario, testing whether you can still identify 'thrash out' despite the added narrative complexity.
quests.exampleSentence: The committee spent all afternoon trying to thrash OUT the budget disagreement, but every time they seemed close to a resolution, someone would raise a new objection.
quests.example: The committee spent all afternoon trying to thrash OUT the budget disagreement, but every time they seemed close to a resolution, someone would raise a new objection.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'OUT' combines with the verb 'THRASH' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative, as before — the phrase describes resolving a disagreement through vigorous, sustained discussion.
quests.nativeTip: This means resolving a heated disagreement through a long, difficult discussion, despite repeated setbacks.
quests.visualAnchor: 🗝️ THRASH + OUT ➔ THRASH OUT

quests.definition: This integrates the media-controversy cluster from earlier in the curriculum, testing whether you can identify 'blow over' as the natural resolution to a scandal that has finally calmed down.
quests.exampleSentence: Even though rumors had been circulating for weeks, the scandal eventually blew OVER once the company issued a public apology.
quests.example: Even though rumors had been circulating for weeks, the scandal eventually blew OVER once the company issued a public apology.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'OVER' combines with the verb 'BLOW' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative, as before — the phrase describes a controversy gradually fading away and being forgotten.
quests.nativeTip: This means a scandal eventually being forgotten after a public apology resolved the tension.
quests.visualAnchor: 🗝️ BLOW + OVER ➔ BLOW OVER

quests.definition: This integrates the resilience and persistence themes from across the curriculum — refusing to 'cave in' despite pressure, and ultimately being vindicated, echoing the idiom about having the last laugh from the previous file.
quests.exampleSentence: No matter how much pressure investors applied, the founder refused to cave IN, and she eventually had the last laugh when the company turned a profit.
quests.example: No matter how much pressure investors applied, the founder refused to cave IN, and she eventually had the last laugh when the company turned a profit.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'IN' combines with the verb 'CAVE' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative, as before — the phrase describes refusing to give up resistance despite sustained pressure.
quests.nativeTip: This means refusing to give in to investor pressure, ultimately being proven right when the company succeeded.
quests.visualAnchor: 🗝️ CAVE + IN ➔ CAVE IN

quests.definition: This final review revisits 'thrash out,' the vigorous, effortful negotiation phrase you've now seen in several realistic contexts throughout your journey through this curriculum.
quests.exampleSentence: Even after the negotiations collapsed twice, the two sides went back to the table and finally thrashed OUT every remaining disagreement before the deadline.
quests.example: Even after the negotiations collapsed twice, the two sides went back to the table and finally thrashed OUT every remaining disagreement before the deadline.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'OUT' combines with the verb 'THRASH' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Figurative, as before — the phrase describes resolving a disagreement through sustained, vigorous discussion.
quests.nativeTip: This means finally resolving a heated disagreement, even though new objections kept disrupting progress.
quests.visualAnchor: 🗝️ THRASH + OUT ➔ THRASH OUT

quests.conceptTitle: Phrasal Anatomy: GET THE HANG OF
quests.definition: 'Get the hang of' means to become comfortable and skilled with something after practice — the very same phrase you first learned back in an earlier stage of this curriculum, now describing your own achievement in mastering phrasal verbs.
quests.exampleSentence: After two hundred levels of practice, she finally felt she had really gotten THE HANG OF using English phrasal verbs naturally in conversation.
quests.example: After two hundred levels of practice, she finally felt she had really gotten THE HANG OF using English phrasal verbs naturally in conversation.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'THE HANG OF' combines with the verb 'GET' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Fully figurative, as before — the phrase describes reaching a comfortable, practiced command of a skill through sustained effort.
quests.nativeTip: This means finally becoming comfortable and skilled with something after a long period of practice, exactly like the process of learning phrasal verbs themselves.
quests.visualAnchor: 🗝️ GET + THE HANG OF ➔ GET THE HANG OF

quests.definition: 'Go the distance' means to persist all the way through a long, demanding task to its completion, without giving up partway. Congratulations — by reaching this final question, you truly have gone the distance in mastering one of English's richest and trickiest areas of vocabulary.
quests.exampleSentence: It took two hundred levels, but you've finally gone THE DISTANCE and mastered one of English's trickiest challenges: phrasal verbs.
quests.example: It took two hundred levels, but you've finally gone THE DISTANCE and mastered one of English's trickiest challenges: phrasal verbs.
quests.particleInsight: The particle 'THE DISTANCE' combines with the verb 'GO' to specialize or transform its action.
quests.literalVsFigurative: Fully figurative, drawn from sports like boxing, where fighters who 'go the distance' complete every scheduled round without being stopped early.
quests.nativeTip: This means seeing a long, demanding task through all the way to the very end.
quests.visualAnchor: 🗝️ GO + THE DISTANCE ➔ GO THE DISTANCE
